threads.body: This is an unusual check. If there was a context leak that triggers this check I'd assume our context leak detector that runs after each test would catch it anyway.

replies.body: Updated in 4c08298b. The JMS 2 and JMS 3 async-send tests passed.

threads.body: Removing the immediate post-`send` assertion loses sender-thread scope-restoration coverage: the callback can still have the correct parent even if `send` leaves its scope current. Keep that assertion inside `runWithSpan`, alongside the new callback-span checks. Same issue in `instrumentation/jms/jms-1.1/javaagent/src/jms2Test/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/jms/v1_1/Jms2InstrumentationTest.java:158`.

replies.body: The callback span doesn't check the sender thread. Both `asyncSendDelayedFailureIsRecorded` tests still check the caller span immediately after the same instrumented `send(Message, CompletionListener)` overload returns normally, before invoking `onException`. That covers the scope-close path without repeating the assertion in the success tests.
